correctness.rationale: For any m>=2 and p>1 the central p-energy minimizer is the unique zero of sum_i w_i |c-f_i|^(p-2)(c-f_i). Its strict coordinate monotonicity and translation covariance place every two-input hub difference strictly between min/max of the leaf difference when that difference is nonconstant, yielding ratio <2. On two leaves, balancing weighted p-forces gives affine center with coefficients w_i^(1/(p-1)), and the exact constant 2 max(alpha_i)/(alpha1+alpha2), attained. At p=2, the weighted arithmetic center has operator norm 2(1-min_i w_i/W), attained by a single high leaf opposite the others. For p>2 and m>=3 a balanced base datum with first residual zero gives derivative weight at leaf1 zero, hence tangent ratio 2. For 1<p<2, balance two nonzero residuals against a vanishing residual on another leaf, making first derivative weight arbitrarily small, hence tangent ratio approaches 2. Every finite pair remains strictly <2. The claimed p=2 jump and continuity for fixed data follow. Independently checked exact p=2 3-leaf value 4/3 and non-Hilbert tangent limits; the checked bundled standard-library program is diagnostic, not the infinite proof.
